To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CR-induced decrease in the ratio of p110alpha to p85alpha/betalike isoforms of PI3-kinase is likely a major mechanism for enhanced insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation and increased glucose transport in skeletal muscle.

calorie restriction [CR; ~60% of ad-libitum intake (AL)] increases the ratio of PI3-kinase (PI3K) catalytic to regulatory isoforms in rat skeletal muscle, and this increase in PI3K catalytic to regulatory activity may contribute to the enhanced insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation and increased glucose transport associated with CR.

calorie restriction increases the ratio catalytic to regulatory isoforms of phosphatidyinositol 3- kinase in skeletal muscle, which favors enhanced insulin signaling and improves insulin-stimulted glucose transport.
